title: Python: service tests
summary: The service suite (46 files, 9,379 lines, 496 tests, 77 parametrize decorators) runs offline by design and tests the right risks. conftest.py blocks sockets at import and drops any inherited OpenRouter key. Model tests go through the real SDK and adapter over httpx.MockTransport, and leak, SSRF, credential, budget and fencing behavior is pinned with planted sentinels and typed codes. Its weakness is that no shared test layer ever formed: the suite defines no pytest fixture at all. As a result, fake OpenRouter replies, catalog payloads, API auth setup, SQL connection fakes and graph builders are copied from file to file, and the provider fakes are copied again in tests/db. The shared fake transport has also drifted to the superseded two-profile policy and refuses Sol. Where production offers no seam, tests subclass LoopMiddleware and ProviderSettings, or build them without running their constructors, and override their private methods. The suite has 38 private touches, 26 of them on these paid-path classes. This makes the paid-path middleware, already a measured hotspot, costly to refactor. The same gap shows in 44 type: ignore comments (24 for fakes, placeholders and patched methods standing in for concrete types, 14 caused by the tests' own loose annotations) and 173 Any annotations. Files are partly organized by the story or review that added them rather than by module. test_worker_inference.py (1,149 lines) spans six production modules under section headings that no longer match, test_final_review.py spans eight, and loop_middleware.py has no test file of its own. Of the other files over 300 lines, test_final_review.py is a structure problem. The rest (route qualification, model policy, workflows, browsing loop, GitHub issues, tool keys, model attempts) are mostly cohesive around one module and would shrink once shared fakes exist, so their size alone is not a finding. Order-dependent global state (a gc-based model check, logging reconfigured without restore) and source-text assertions are the remaining risks. Duplication with tests/db is limited to the fake provider builders: the split between offline tests and disposable-database checks is deliberate and documented in module docstrings. Findings come from reading code and read-only tool runs; no test was run.

scores.why: The project's ruff and mypy strict runs pass on tests, but nothing enforces pytest-style, private-access or local-import rules (47 function-level imports, 16 private accesses), async style is split between asyncio.run and pytest-asyncio, and DH-06's controlled clocks are not used everywhere.

Two helper modules exist (conftest.py, fake_openrouter.py) but are imported through pytest's sys.path insertion, test_tool_catalog.py imports helpers from test_api.py, and there is no support package, so helpers live wherever they were first needed.
Functions are short (8 over 40 lines), but test_worker_inference.py is 1,149 lines, nine files exceed 300 lines, and a fake's __call__ and one test run 86 and 102 lines.

Most tests check one behavior with a clear arrange, act and assert. A few helpers mix patching, building and running (bind_with, call, real_attempt), and one test helper copies the runner's block logic.
Most files map to one module, but some are filed by story or review (test_final_review.py, parts of test_worker_inference.py), so loop_middleware's tests sit in six files and pricing tests in four.

Transport-level fakes under the real SDK are a model approach, but paid-path internals are tested by overriding private methods, SQL fakes match on substrings with silent defaults, and some wiring is checked by searching source text.

Every file has a docstring giving its scope, its story or decision and where the live or disposable counterpart runs. The section headings in test_worker_inference.py and the two-profile docstring in fake_openrouter.py are stale, and a few comments are hard to parse (test_operation_values.py:84-85).
mypy strict covers tests and passes, but 44 type: ignore comments and 173 Any annotations mean fakes and helpers are not checked against the production signatures they stand in for.

Failures are asserted by typed code or failure class almost everywhere. Only 3 broad pytest.raises and 2 raises(Exception, match=...) remain, and a few tests convert exceptions to strings to work around the gc-based check.
Coverage of risky logic is strong and offline, but the lack of fixtures, the copied fakes, coupling to private internals and order-dependent global state make the suite costly to change.
A careful, well-documented suite without a shared layer: adding a profile, route, SQL query or middleware refactor means editing several copies or several private overrides.

strengths.title: Network and provider key are blocked for the whole session, and tests prove it
strengths.evidence: conftest.py:10 removes OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and lines 23-27 replace socket connect, connect_ex, sendto, create_connection and getaddrinfo at import, so third-party import-time code also runs under the block. test_model_transport.py:50-54 shows that a real-looking key still ends in SocketBlockedError, and test_app_factory.py:11-15 and test_contracts.py:162-168 prove the block is in force, as model-gateway.md requires.

strengths.title: Fakes sit at the HTTP transport, under the real SDK and adapter
strengths.evidence: test_model_attempts.py:247-271 proves the SDK retries neither a 5xx nor a connection error, and lines 274-298 check the read timeout the SDK actually sends. test_worker_inference.py:355-364 asserts the model, max_tokens and provider routing flags on the wire, and test_route_qualification.py:226-234 checks every request the paid runner sends. Faking at the transport covers serialization and client configuration that a mocked client would skip.

strengths.title: Leak tests use planted sentinels across every output channel
strengths.evidence: test_worker_inference.py:582-598 plants reply text in an SDK exception and proves it reaches no log field. test_result_stream.py:117-126 keeps reasoning, plan arguments and private paths out of notifications. test_reasoning_trial.py:214-227 checks the report, the ledger and caplog. test_operation_values.py:224-236 scans the status body for paths, hosts and secrets.

strengths.title: Architecture rules are enforced by AST and source scans
strengths.evidence: test_model_policy.py:355-374 fails if any module other than factory.py imports an inference SDK. test_api.py:201-209 forbids background work in request handlers. test_route_qualification.py:346-355 forbids strict-output requests in application code, per Decision 0005.

strengths.title: Docstrings and names state scope, source and where the rest is proven
strengths.evidence: test_github_issues.py:1 points to tests/db/connector_check.py for the gateway, test_credentials.py:1 and test_model_attempts.py:1 point to scripts/app_db.py, and test_browser_executor.py:1-5 points to the Docker qualifier. test_environment.py:1-5 states what it does not claim. Test names read as behavior, for example test_a_401_for_a_key_replaced_mid_call_leaves_its_successor_alone at test_worker_inference.py:954.

strengths.title: Injected clocks and sleepers wherever production offers the seam
strengths.evidence: test_wake_clock.py:6-12 drives both clocks by hand. test_model_attempts.py:79-85 records RetryPolicy sleeps against a fixed now. test_browsing_loop.py:164-171 feeds clock ticks. test_worker_inference.py:197-215 advances CatalogCache's clock across the refresh boundary.

strengths.title: Shared fixture files drive boundary validation in both languages
strengths.evidence: test_contracts.py:30 and 61-75 run every case in contracts/fixtures/boundary-cases.json and check that each required kind is covered. test_credentials.py:34 and 39-49 run credential-precedence.json. contracts.md asks for exactly this kind of shared fixture.

strengths.title: Protocol seams let fakes type-check with no ignore
strengths.evidence: Membership (test_api.py:29-37) satisfies MembershipStore (api/security.py:14), FakePool (test_api.py:159-168) satisfies the app's Pool protocol (api/app.py:30), and Pages (test_browsing_loop.py:40-54) satisfies browsing_loop.Page (browsing_loop.py:59). None of them needs a type: ignore, unlike the fakes for concrete classes.

findings.title: Paid-path tests replace private LoopMiddleware and ProviderSettings internals instead of using seams

locations.note: Busy skips __init__, overrides _guard, _sleep and _admitted_call, and calls _with_slot, although the constructor takes sleep= and slot_wait_seconds=
Refusing overrides _guard and _admitted_call and calls _summarize
Stopping overrides _guard, _compacted, _with_slot and _repair
Builds LoopMiddleware with __new__ and assigns _guard and _compacted
Settings(ProviderSettings) skips __init__, sets self._store = self and overrides _effective_environment, _settings_row and _record
Patches ProviderSettings.__init__ to a no-op
Sets the private ContextVar _ADMITTED; also at test_worker_inference.py:1133-1139, and _MIDDLEWARE at test_browsing_tool.py:235
The constructor needs connection, scope, limits and route. _guard reads ownership from the connection, and _admitted_call builds ModelAdmission(self._connection) itself at lines 577, 589 and 594

findings.evidence:
To swap out private steps, tests subclass production classes or build them without running their constructors. test_worker_inference.py:770-786:
```python
class Busy(LoopMiddleware):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._slot_wait_seconds = 30.0
    async def _guard(self) -> float:
        return 1.0
    async def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        waits.append(seconds)
```
The constructor already accepts sleep= and slot_wait_seconds= (loop_middleware.py:357-358). But _guard checks ownership over the connection, and _admitted_call constructs its own admission ledger, so Refusing, Busy and Stopping skip __init__ and override _guard, _admitted_call, _sleep, _compacted, _with_slot and _repair. ProviderSettings builds its own credential store (provider_settings.py:85-88), so tests subclass it, set self._store = self and override its private row methods. Three files set the private ContextVars _ADMITTED and _MIDDLEWARE. Counted across the suite: 16 private-member accesses (ruff --select SLF001 on tests/), 16 private names imported from autobots in 8 files (an ast scan of the import statements) and 6 classes subclassed or built without running __init__, 38 in all. 26 of them reach into the paid path: 15 of the SLF001 hits (LoopMiddleware, its two ContextVars, ProviderSettings, CatalogCache and AttemptModel), the 5 loop_middleware helpers imported by name (_charged, _failure_without_status, _finished, _retry_after and _streamed) and the 6 constructor bypasses. The other 12 touch workflow_runner, tool_gateway, runs, goal_loop, domain.workflows and the route qualifier's _main.
findings.impact: loop_middleware.py is 674 lines, and _admitted_call is a measured hotspot (C901 15, PLR0915 65; the constructor takes 10 parameters, PLR0913), so it is a likely refactor target. Any behavior-preserving extraction there would break the tests for budget refusal during compaction, busy-slot waits and cut-off repair at the same moment, for example moving slot waits or summaries into collaborators, renaming a private method, or turning _sleep into a collaborator. The fast, offline safety net disappears exactly where paid calls are admitted. The disposable db checks (tests/db/goal_loop_check.py, memory_check.py and admission_check.py) still drive the real middleware, but only on the db profile. Because the subclasses skip __init__, a new attribute read on these paths raises AttributeError only in tests, and the tests keep passing against overridden steps even when the real guard or admission changes. ProviderSettings' key-rejection and run-intent tests have the same problem.
findings.recommendation:
Add seams, then test through public methods. Write the seam-based tests next to the current ones before deleting the overrides.
- LoopMiddleware: inject the per-dispatch guard and the admission ledger as keyword-only arguments whose defaults keep today's database-backed behavior, so no production call site passes them. Use the existing sleep=, slot_wait_seconds= and summary_route= parameters. Add public context managers for the two ContextVars, as result_stream already does with use_tap and reset_tap.
- Pure reply helpers: make _charged, _finished, _retry_after and _failure_without_status public in a small module.
- ProviderSettings: accept the credential store and a settings-row reader as optional constructor arguments.
- CatalogCache: it already takes now=, so drive staleness with a clock, as test_worker_inference.py:197-215 does, instead of writing _snapshot and _fetch.
- Reuse the in-memory Ledger at test_model_attempts.py:50-72 as the admission fake, adding the reconcile and record_reply methods that _admitted_call also calls.
- Run ruff SLF001 on tests with today's count as a baseline, so new private access shows up in review.
findings.sketch:
adapters/loop_middleware.py
  LoopMiddleware(connection, scope, limits, route, *, guard: Guard | None = None,
                 admission: Callable[[], Admission] | None = None, sleep=..., slot_wait_seconds=..., ...)
    Guard = Callable[[], Awaitable[float]]   # default: today's ownership and time-left check
    Admission: Protocol                       # default: ModelAdmission(connection)
  admitted_scope(), active_middleware(m)    # public context managers for _ADMITTED and _MIDDLEWARE
adapters/model_replies.py                    # charged, finished, retry_after, failure_without_status, reply_facts
application/provider_settings.py
  ProviderSettings(connection, context, *, store: CredentialStore | None = None, rows: SettingsRows | None = None)
tests/support/middleware.py
  middleware(guard=..., admission=Ledger(), sleep=recorder)   # builds the real class with fakes
findings.ruleCheck: python-worker.md and DH-06 ask for tests of ownership, cancellation and budget behavior through injected collaborators, and model-gateway.md requires budget reservations and concurrency limits to be enforced. The seams default to today's guard and admission, so no lease, fence or budget check is weakened (ground rule 2). Only how tests reach them changes. Tests come first because this is a paid path. The new arguments are keyword-only, default to today's guard and ModelAdmission, and stay unset at every production call site.
findings.verifierNote: All eight locations and the ruff measures match (SLF001 16, C901 15, PLR0915 65, PLR0913 10), but 12 of the 38 private touches are outside the paid path, so occurrences are now the 26 on LoopMiddleware, ProviderSettings, CatalogCache and AttemptModel. The impact now notes that the db profile still drives the real middleware, and the Ledger fake needs reconcile and record_reply.

Counted with grep:
- 8 hand-written "object": "chat.completion" bodies: six in service tests (also test_route_qualification.py:148-172) and two in tests/db (product_inference_worker.py:195, sleep_inference_worker.py:54).

findings.recommendation: NOW comes from the wall clock because prepared() and InferenceSource._input_rate read datetime.now(UTC) themselves (worker_inference.py:131 and 295), so a fixed NOW alone would make every fixture catalog stale. Give prepared() the now= parameter that prepare_attempt already takes, and InferenceSource a clock that defaults to the wall clock, as CatalogCache does. Then fix NOW to a constant and pass that clock to every CatalogCache and InferenceSource. Give ResultTap and timed_catalog a monotonic parameter that defaults to time.monotonic, and drive them with a fake clock in tests. Keep one real-time timeout test for guarded_fetch, with a comment saying why.

findings.impact: A file's dependencies aren't visible at its top, and re-imports shadow names already in scope. The conftest and helper imports would break under pytest's importlib import mode, or when a file is run any other way.
